In addition to the January 29, 2020 FOMC’s on-hold, modestly dovish macro tone (strong labor market, moderate growth, below-target inflation) and the Financial Stability Report’s caution on elevated leverage and stretched risk-asset valuations, the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to a tightening credit channel that tempers the outlook further. SLOOS indicates banks tightened standards and other terms on C&I loans (including for medium-market firms) and construction/land development CRE, raised credit score thresholds and tightened credit limits, and reduced loan granting; demand was generally unchanged-to-weaker for several consumer and CRE categories. Banks also reported reduced risk tolerance and expect tighter standards for riskier loans, alongside anticipated deterioration in collateral values and some loan portfolios. This combination suggests headwinds to capex and credit-sensitive sectors and reinforces a cautious, stay-on-hold stance with a dovish risk-management bias, but it also softens the otherwise positive macro read.

Net assessment updated: modestly dovish but more constrained by tightening credit conditions; sentiment nudged lower.
